unreleased: Leaving a Daily in progress no longer asks first, and the home screen confirms it is saved.
The Back button during a game now goes home, closing any open popup or the menu first.
Changing tab and toggling a filter chip now give a light tap of haptic feedback.
A game that unlocks several achievements now shows them together on one screen.
The last screen of a game now shows events placed, the day's place, and the way home.
Each end-of-game screen now moves on with a Continue button.
The bottom bar's buttons no longer show through the end-of-game screens.
The game-over card keeps Continue on screen after submitting on a small phone.

notes: The end of a game now gathers the timeline into a gallery of its paintings.
A shared result now shows every painting on the timeline as a collage.
Card art now spreads across each card and fades into its colour.
The card in hand is now a square showing its whole painting.
Curated themes now open with a short introduction and a fact about the day's theme.
Every achievement now unlocks a new avatar, ready to wear on the leaderboard from the Profile page.
The menu now has a Profile page where players can change their leaderboard name.
Players can now pick an animal avatar for the daily leaderboard.
The top three players on the daily leaderboard now stand out with larger portraits.
The portrait beside the leaderboard name box now opens the avatar picker.
Forty-four more cards that showed the wrong picture or a framed mockup now have new artwork.
Three duplicate cards were retired and several confusing card descriptions were corrected.
Twenty-six cards with wrong or flawed pictures now have new artwork.
The Archive now lists every daily from the last 30 days, and a missed day can be played to keep a streak.
A cleared themed deck now earns a gold trophy, and the Daily card names its curated theme.
Card popups now have a close button beside a narrower report button, within thumb reach.
Custom filters and the country picker gain Select all and Clear buttons, and every chip shows a tick or a cross.
Custom games can now include or leave out individual countries within a region.
Daily themes now include regions, countries and pairings such as Art in Italy.
The iPhone app is now ready for iOS 27 and opens normally on it.
Custom games can now be filtered by world region, such as Europe or East Asia.
Names, dates and descriptions were corrected on over a hundred cards, and 33 duplicate cards were removed.
A daily challenge left part-way now resumes where it stopped instead of dealing again.
Curated themes now arrive every Monday and Friday, with twenty-two new decks from pharaohs to pirates.
The app has a new painted hourglass icon and a matching launch screen.
Hundreds more events now cover a span of years rather than a single date.
Another 92 event dates were corrected against their sources.
The Daily card gains an eye button that reopens today's finished timeline.
Some events now cover a span of years rather than a single date, and a card placed inside that span counts as correct.
Around 270 event dates were corrected against their sources.
Every card now carries two paragraphs of background, readable once the card is placed.
The timeline grew a rail that stretches with the board, and a marker that lands as its tick.
Short hints now appear as the game teaches itself, and Reset Hints brings them back.
Past daily decks moved to an Archive tab, and the Stats page was rebuilt around it.
Nineteen curated decks arrived, from plagues and clockwork to ciphers and assassinations.
522 duplicate events left the deck, so the same card stops turning up twice.
Card text no longer gives away the year it is asking about.
Daily puzzles can now run a hand-picked theme, named on the day it plays.
374 sporting events joined the catalogue as a category of their own.
Sharing a result now attaches a card from the run instead of a wall of text.
The daily leaderboard shows every player, not just the top of the table.
Decks now open easy and ramp up, instead of shuffling at random.
A card that looks wrong can be reported from its detail view.
A wrong placement now pulses across the screen and the board follows the card.
The iOS app can send a daily reminder when the new puzzle is ready.
A card lost to a wrong guess leaves a tombstone on the timeline.
Stats and achievements arrived, tracking streaks, accuracy and games played.
